outcome: Close G20 and D2: the expression language reads the SQL cast spellings agents write, try_cast and ::, with their own semantics; the other SQL constructs a semantic expression cannot hold are refused with advice naming what to write instead; and a cast in group_by is no longer split as an alias.
criteria: Expressions read try_cast(expression as type), resolving to a new try_cast expression that compiles to DuckDB TRY_CAST so a value that does not convert becomes NULL, and expression::type as a strict cast; the existing cast expression and the idempotency fingerprints of existing requests are unchanged.
A parse error caused by a backtick identifier, EXTRACT of a year, month or day, ILIKE, or LIKE applied to a function result carries advice whose rewrite, sent as-is, succeeds.

A parse error caused by CASE, a window function or a scalar subquery carries advice naming raw_query, with the step rewritten as a raw_query first step when the expression sits in the transform's first step and reads only the source, and an explanation without a rewrite otherwise.
An expression with as inside parentheses, such as cast(x as double), is not split as expression-as-alias in group_by, select or derive, while expression as name still names the result.

Tests on data unrelated to any benchmark cover each accepted form and each advised refusal, with every rewrite sent back and its rows checked; the transform tool description and README name try_cast and ::; the full suite including the boundary tests passes; and a pull request against Intentum main states the changes, their evidence and tradeoffs.

reason: Adding try_cast showed that a strict cast which meets a value it cannot convert fails at execution with no advice; once the language teaches cast, that failure is the next dead end, and PR #3's join advice still points to TRY_CAST in a raw_query although the grammar now has it.
criteria: A transform that fails at execution because a cast met a value it cannot convert carries advice whose rewrite uses try_cast in place of cast and, sent as-is, succeeds; the join key-type advice names try_cast in a derive as the way round a key that does not convert.

note: Expressions read try_cast(expression as type) as a new TryCastExpr node compiled to TRY_CAST (a blank or n/a becomes null where cast fails) and expression::type as a strict cast; CastExpr keeps its fields, held by a test, so existing fingerprints are unchanged. New advice: sql_spelling respells backtick names and EXTRACT of year, month or day; like_as_function now covers ILIKE and LIKE on a function result; sql_in_expression rewrites CASE, a window function (as QUALIFY) or a scalar subquery in the first filter or single-name derive that reads only input as a raw_query first step and explains otherwise, including a subquery over another dataset and a later step; cast_conversion rewrites a transform that failed on a conversion error with try_cast in place of cast and ::. The #3 join advice now names try_cast in a derive. The alias split only takes an as with balanced parentheses on its left and a parenthesis-free name on its right, so cast(quantity as double) in group_by gets group_by's own naming refusal and hint, and a named cast still names the column. Ten tests on examples/orders.csv and a four-row text amounts CSV send every rewrite back and check its rows; nine fail with the fix stashed, the tenth is the CastExpr field guard. The tool description and README name try_cast and ::. 381 tests pass including the boundary tests. Pull request #4 states the changes, evidence and tradeoffs.
